reproducibility_correction.observed_issue: A later rerun reproduced all headline and regime-level scientific quantities but produced a different JSON result SHA because disturbance-family total-variation terms were accumulated by iterating an unordered Python set.
reproducibility_correction.cause: Python hash randomization changed the floating-point addition order in family-TV accumulation at the least-significant-bit level.
reproducibility_correction.fix: Sort disturbance-family labels before total-variation summation; no weights, grid, comparators, metrics, estimators, seeds or interpretation rules changed.
reproducibility_correction.determinism_gate: Full 864-regime benchmark executed twice with PYTHONHASHSEED=1 and 987654; result JSON and all three CSV hashes were byte-identical.

interpretation.primary: Frozen V6 is the most robust fixed targeted policy across unknown regimes in this abstract benchmark, but it is not the per-regime optimum.
interpretation.failure_boundary: Common event prevalence and strongly shared residual structure enlarge the failure region; at event prevalence 0.90 the mean V6 joint ratio is below uniform.
interpretation.same_alpha: The best same-alpha policy changes sharply with prevalence, demonstrating that exploration alone does not explain all gains but separate quotas are not universally optimal either.
interpretation.ecological_inference: The exploration-only prevalence estimator is nearly unbiased across prevalence regimes; the naive selected-sample estimator is positively biased, especially when events are rare. The exploration estimator pays a variance cost when prevalence is high.
interpretation.tv: The V8 maximum V6 disturbance-family TV is 0.395125, below the theorem's 0.5 half-exploration bound but above the V4/V7 empirical 0.25 criterion in many regimes. Therefore 0.25 must not be presented as a general theoretical guarantee.
